clue.text: Bank covering a trendy bachelor's colourful display

indicators.note: the bank, as a covering, goes round the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: a bank of seats or switches is a row of them
in means fashionable
B is the standard abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: A riverbank sheltering a fashionable single man shows off something bright.
explanation.definitionFit: An arc of spectral colours across the sky is nature's most colourful display.

clue.text: Defeated Republican exposed

parts.note: outed means publicly exposed

explanation.surface: A politician beaten after being publicly unmasked.
explanation.definitionFit: Being routed means suffering a heavy, decisive defeat.

clue.text: Excite father keeping piano at home at first

indicators.note: at first places the home word at the front of the rest

parts.note: in means at home

indicators.note: father keeps piano, holding it within

parts.note: to sire is to father; a sire is a father
p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

explanation.surface: Dad thrills everyone by keeping a piano in the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire someone is to stir or arouse them, a close synonym of excite.

clue.text: Game secured by beauty holding a gun

indicators.note: the beauty holds the other pieces inside her

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman
gat is slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A game protected by a pretty woman with a pistol.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a table game rolling balls into holes, so an example of a game.

clue.text: Who, say, understands women's yen to be tribal magician?

indicators.note: read as stands under: in a down light this piece goes below the others

parts.note: W abbreviates women
a yen is an itch, a longing
Doctor Who, the time-travelling TV character, is an example of a doctor

explanation.surface: The Doctor grasps a woman's craving to become a shaman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Understands' splits as 'under stands', placing the doctor below WITCH in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A healer believed to wield supernatural power within a tribe is a magician of sorts.

clue.text: Friction mark made by second class surgeon

parts.note: B denotes the second grade or class
Joseph Lister, the pioneer of antiseptic surgery

explanation.surface: A wound left by a mediocre surgeon.
explanation.walkthrough: Lister is the famous Victorian surgeon who introduced antiseptics.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubbing raises a fluid-filled bubble on the skin, a typical mark caused by friction.

clue.text: Youngster exchanging ring for a horse

indicators.note: exchanging one thing for another swaps the ring out and the a in

parts.note: a boy is a youngster
a ring is round like the letter O

explanation.surface: A child trades a ring for a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A reddish-brown horse with black points is called a bay.

clue.text: Old Peruvians cut down to be on the safe side

indicators.note: cut down means trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.words: to be on the safe side
parts.note: in case means as a precaution

explanation.surface: Ancient Peruvians felled trees as a precaution.
explanation.definitionFit: The empire of these Andean people ruled Peru before the Spanish conquest.

clue.text: Sightseer in ancient city is feeding small child

indicators.note: feeding into means going inside, so these go within the child

parts.note: a tot is a small child
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: A visitor in an old city feeds a little one.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor seeing the sights is a holidaymaker, a direct synonym.

clue.text: A peak return time, hourly on and off, on circular route?

indicators.note: a return goes back, so the words a peak are read backwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky peak

indicators.note: on and off takes every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A mountain trip timetable with buses each hour, intermittently, on a loop.
explanation.walkthrough: The final 'on' links wordplay to definition; 'circular route?' hints at something going round.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that goes round in a circle, revolving or rotating, describes a circular route.

clue.text: Ugly students' leader visiting university at regular intervals

indicators.note: the visitor comes inside the host word, so the letter sits within it

parts.note: nightly means every night, so at regular intervals

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A student union head is unsightly when touring campus on a schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At regular intervals' looks like an alternate-letter instruction but is the synonym NIGHTLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unpleasant to look at is ugly; the two words are plain synonyms.

clue.text: Foolishly invite love, in short

indicators.note: the zero for love is placed inside the word for short

parts.note: curt means brief or short
love is nil in tennis, the letter O

explanation.surface: Rashly asking for love, briefly put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' looks like part of the definition (to woo); it is the tennis O.
explanation.definitionFit: To court disaster or danger is to invite it recklessly, an idiomatic sense.

clue.text: Electoral system rejected by divine law

indicators.note: the electoral system is thrown out of the word for divine

parts.note: to divine is to foretell or predict
PR is proportional representation, a voting system

explanation.surface: A voting method spurned by heavenly law.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' reads as the adjective holy, but is the verb meaning to foretell.
explanation.definitionFit: An official decree or proclamation has the force of law.

clue.text: Shock, meeting religious leader in this crude garment

parts.note: a shock is a thick mass of hair

indicators.note: the religious leader's letter goes inside the crude word

parts.note: a crude, vulgar word for rubbish or excrement

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: A startling encounter with a cleric wearing rough clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' suggests surprise but means a mop of hair; 'this crude' signals a vulgar word.
explanation.definitionFit: A coarse cloth shirt worn by penitents and ascetics is a kind of garment.

clue.text: Eg Cambodian don struggling with his niece

indicators.note: struggling suggests the letters thrash about into a new order

explanation.surface: A university lecturer battles with his niece, a Cambodian.
explanation.definitionFit: Cambodia lies in the Southeast Asian peninsula once called French Indochina, so a Cambodian is an example.

clue.text: Consider proficient land-agent's sense of well-being

parts.note: to feel is to think or consider
good at something means proficient
in Scotland a factor is the agent who manages an estate

explanation.surface: Think of a capable estate manager's contentment.
explanation.walkthrough: A factor is the Scottish term for a land agent managing an estate.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes the general optimism and contentment people feel, especially about the economy.

clue.text: Constructed a place for officers over fifty in base

indicators.note: in a down clue, over turns the mess upside down

parts.note: the mess is where officers eat

indicators.note: fifty goes inside the base

parts.note: a bed is a base or foundation
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An officers' mess built for someone over fifty at a military base.
explanation.definitionFit: Put together from parts, or built, matches constructed.

clue.text: Musician swapping article with one in bulky journal?

indicators.note: swapping trades the article and one between the two words

parts.note: big means bulky
I is the Roman numeral one
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: with carries the second half of the swap, the other letter going back

parts.note: a journal is a newspaper, a paper

explanation.surface: A musician trades features in a fat magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: In BIG PAPER the I and the A trade places.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the bagpipes is a musician.

clue.text: In dentures, say? They are required for one to be served

definitions.text: In dentures, say? They are required for one to be served

parts.words: In dentures, say? They are required for one to be served
parts.note: indentures are the contracts binding a trainee to a master; the trainee serves the term they set

explanation.surface: False teeth needed before anyone is given a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Split as 'In dentures' the word seems about teeth; joined, indentures are the trade-training contracts one serves.
explanation.definitionFit: Indentures are the written agreements under which a trainee's period of learning a trade is served.

clue.text: Bloomer Auntie foolishly made under pressure

indicators.note: in a down light the shuffled letters sit below the pressure letter

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: foolishly suggests the letters behave wildly and get mixed

explanation.surface: Auntie made a silly mistake under stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder (or knickers), but here it means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer, something that blooms, is a flower such as this garden annual.

clue.text: Dressed like soldiers capturing key slope

indicators.note: capturing holds the key inside

parts.note: soldiers dress in line, aligned on parade
C is a musical key

explanation.surface: Troops in formation seize a key hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising gradient or slope is an incline.

clue.text: Top of acacia waves about in north wind

indicators.note: the waves go about, round the tree's first letter

parts.note: bores are tidal waves surging up a river

indicators.note: the top of a word in a down light is its first letter

explanation.surface: A treetop sways in the north wind.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology this god personified the north wind.

clue.text: Source of perfume turning up prior to …

indicators.note: turning the letters over and about rearranges them

explanation.surface: A fragrance appears before the next clue continues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turning up' looks like a phrase meaning arriving, but 'turning' is the anagram signal and 'up prior to' the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowl of dried petals and spices scents a room, making it a source of fragrance.

clue.text: Female leaving western island, a native of Muscat?

indicators.note: the western letter departs from the word for female

parts.note: a woman is a female

explanation.surface: A woman quits a western isle to become a Muscat local.
explanation.walkthrough: Muscat is the capital of Oman, though the name also suggests a grape.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is the capital of Oman, so a native of it is from that country.

clue.text: … virile former chairman entertaining honoured companion

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold, so the honour sits inside the chairman

parts.note: Chairman Mao, the late Chinese leader
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A manly ex-boss hosts a decorated friend.
explanation.walkthrough: CH is the post-nominal of the Companion of Honour, a British award.
explanation.definitionFit: Aggressively masculine and virile are close synonyms describing a manly man.

clue.text: Sharp pain delivered by a knife in Africa

parts.note: a pang is a sudden sharp pain

explanation.surface: A stab of pain inflicted by a blade in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a broad-bladed machete-style tool used in East Africa.

clue.text: Recipient of information a woman will approve of?

definitions.meaning: British slang for the ear, from the phrase 'a word in your ear' said with a seashell comparison
read as a contraction: she will be pleased with it

explanation.surface: A tip-off a lady is bound to welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: SHELL-LIKE is British slang for the ear ('a word in your shell-like'); split as SHE'LL LIKE it is what a woman will approve of.
explanation.definitionFit: The ear receives what one is told, and the playful split gives a woman's approval.

clue.text: The girl to take to 10!

definitions.meaning: to take to court, the answer to 10 across

explanation.surface: That woman is to be taken to court.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name, and the verb meaning to bring legal action against someone.

clue.text: Make about a shilling cutting pork pie

parts.note: re means about or concerning

indicators.note: the shilling cuts into the fib, sitting inside it

parts.note: rhyming slang: pork pie means lie
S was the abbreviation for the old shilling coin

explanation.surface: Turn a small profit on a pork pie by slicing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pork pie' is Cockney rhyming slang for a lie; S stands for the shilling, a pre-decimal British coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a sum, as in a sale making a profit, is to realise it.

clue.text: Ring-like? Some may think Wagner's is!

definitions.meaning: like a ring, a loop with no end
a joke at Wagner's Ring cycle, four very long operas

explanation.surface: Circular, as some say Wagner's operatic cycle seems.
explanation.definitionFit: A loop has no terminus, and Wagner's Ring operas famously seem interminable.
